I grew up with this FF3, but never really understood these ambiguous buff items: earrings, hyper wrist, atlas armlet, and hero ring. Do they actually do anything? It's hard to tell, especially when you're 10 and not good at paying attention to ridiculous, mostly useless details like this. I played through one last time (though probably not the last last time) a year ago, and just now found this table in my notes, which gives a sampling of damage scores for a few of Sabin's attacks given different relics.

attack damage
earrings+hyper wrist  
fight 372
pummel 429
aura 547
earrings+earrings  
fight 303
pummel 374
aura 698
atlas armlet+earrings  
fight 332
pummel 482
aura 574
gauntlet+earrings  
fight 315
pummel 368
aura 538
hero ring+earrings  
fight 416
pummel 492
aura 687
hero ring+hyper wrist  
fight 479
pummel 540
aura 533

This was enough information for my purposes. Double earrings raises his aurabolt by around 30%— though I neglected to get a proper baseline for the damage on that attack. You may be surprised to know that Sabin's attacks aren't all keyed on strength: only pummel and suplex depend on Vigor while the rest depend on magic power.

I'm still curious how much of the differentials are down to randomness? What do these items actually do?

Fortunately, I'm aware of the algorithms FAQ, and that people have reverse-engineered pretty much anything that can possibly be known about this game, so I checked that. Hopefully whoever wrote that knew his 6502 ASM...

 Step 2a. If physical attack and attacker is equipped with Atlas Armlet or
 Hero Ring:

 Damage = Damage * 5/4

 Step 2b. If magical attack and attacker is equipped with 1 Earring or
 Hero Ring:

 Damage = Damage * 5/4 

 Step 2c. If magical attack and attacker is equipped with 2 Earrings / Hero
 Rings:

 Damage = Damage + (Damage / 4) + (Damage / 4)

In other words, AA and HR do the same thing except that AA is only physical whereas HR is also magical. Also, these items are idempotent. The exact bonuses for these things is 1/4 for each equipped.

The hyper wrist is different from either of those items in that it increases vigor by 50%. As the FAQ explains, damage is calculated as ((level^2 * (vigor*2 + bat.pow)) / 256) * 3 / 2 with the caveat that vigor is capped at 255.

So if Sabin is level 15 with a battle power of, say, 80, and vigor of 50, he'd do 221±12.

What, then, would be better: 50% more vigor + 25% more damage, or 50% more damage?

cl-user> (+ (damage 15 80 75) (* (damage 15 80 75) 0.25))
379.02832
cl-user> (+ (damage 15 80 50) (* (damage 15 80 50) 0.50))
355.95703

The difference is barely more than random variance. With these inputs, the hyper wrist+hero ring combo is better than double hero ring, but that only applies to the fight command; blitzes substitute their own battle power, such that pummel = 110, aurabolt = 68 and Suplex = 180, according to the FAQ. So for Suplex's relatively high BP, double hero ring is better where the same may not be the case for Pummel. But again, the difference is hard to notice. And aurabolt is probably better anyway.

I think that's as much as I care to muck around with this bullshit. Hope you enjoyed the vidja science.
